title: Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Amendment (Corrective Services Authorities) Bill 2022
short_title: Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Amendment (Corrective Services Authorities) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let state and territory corrective services authorities access telecommunications data under existing federal law after receiving a declaration from the Commonwealth minister.
A declaration would require a request from the relevant state or territory minister and could impose conditions limiting which data access powers an authority used.
Declared authorities would remain subject to existing access thresholds, reporting obligations and Commonwealth Ombudsman oversight, with the legislation beginning the day after royal assent.
changes: A new declaration mechanism would give corrective services authorities enforcement agency status without the existing temporary declaration limit.
The Commonwealth minister would have to revoke a declaration when the relevant state or territory minister requested it.
The Commonwealth minister could also revoke access where an authority's compliance with the legislation was unsatisfactory.
summary.affected: State and territory corrective services authorities, telecommunications data subjects, responsible ministers and the Commonwealth Ombudsman would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Tim Wilson
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act to allow corrective services authorities to access telecommunications data to combat illicit mobile phone use in prisons, implementing a recommendation from the comprehensive review of the national intelligence community's legal framework. A temporary declaration under section 176A has already given Corrective Services NSW this access, and Operation Ironside has resulted in over 350 individuals being charged.
